thread.title: Men posed with guns on Snapchat 18 minutes after South Carolina killing, prosecutors say - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Men posed with guns on Snapchat 18 minutes after South Carolina killing, prosecutors say - NewsBreak

author: Noah Feit
title: Men posed with guns on Snapchat 18 minutes after South Carolina killing, prosecutors say - NewsBreak
text:
By Noah Feit ,
17 hours ago The 9th Circuit Solicitor’s Office said a jury found two men guilty of murder following the 2023 shooting death of another man in Charleston County, SC. Getty Images A South Carolina jury recently found two men guilty of murder, according to the 9th Circuit Solicitor’s Office .
On Oct. 9, both Qutairus Capers-Mitchell and Ti’Zaveis Grampus were convicted of murdering Emmanuel Johnson in 2023, the solicitor’s office said in a news release.
Capers-Mitchell also was found guilty of possession of a weapon during the commission of a violent crime, according to the release.
The 4-day trial in a Charleston County courtroom ended with the jury finding Capers-Mitchell and Grampus guilty, the solicitor’s office said. Judge Roger Young sentenced Capers-Mitchell to 45 years in prison, according to the release.
Grampus’ sentence was deferred until a pre-sentence report will be completed, the solicitor’s office said.
The convictions are connected to a June 4, 2023 shooting, according to the release. Just before 5 a.m. on that day, Capers-Mitchell and Grampus canvased the North Charleston area before ambushing Johnson, the solicitor’s office said. They backed down a road to lie in wait before firing numerous times at the victim who was standing outside an apartment building, according to the release.
There was no word about a motive for the shooting, or any connection between the victim and the gunmen.
Capers-Mitchell posted images of himself and a third co-defendant, Bernard Brown on Snapchat 18 minutes after Johnson was killed, the solicitor’s office said. They posed flashing their guns which were later recovered by law enforcement officers, according to the release. Those guns matched spent shell casings from the scene, the solicitor’s office said.
Grampus was seen on surveillance footage before and after the homicide, according to the release. Investigators matched his fingerprints to multiple items found in the getaway vehicle, the solicitor’s office said.
Brown, the third defendant, pleaded guilty to murder and possession of a weapon during the commission of a violent crime on the first day of the trial, according to the release. Judge Young sentenced Brown to 30 years in prison.
Special Counsel Stephanie Linder, Assistant Solicitor Ashley Errett along with Solicitor’s Investigator Dustin Morris prosecuted the case.
Attorneys Justin Kata and Jason Bybee were listed as Grampus’ lawyers, Charleston County court records show. Mary Ford was listed as Capers-Mitchell’s attorney, while Brian Byrd served as Brown’s lawyer, according to court records.
